- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from 3rd day onward with sentiment-weighted smoothing.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 2–5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) if sentiment is bullish; add 2–5% buffer to final 7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of lagged price adjustment to forecast.
